Turnstiles facilitate efficient mutex management in the Solaris operating system by decoupling lock state from the mutex itself. This design enables fine-grained locking with minimal memory overhead and provides a mechanism for handling priority inversion. The Bitap algorithm, also known as the shift-and algorithm, detects pattern occurrences in a text stream using bitwise operations. It represents the set of active matching states as a bitset, updating potential matches through left-shifts and bitwise AND operations as each character is processed.
